beats.title: The Subscriber Era Begins
beats.body: Subscriptions turn YouTube from a video archive into a leaderboard; early comedy channels like Smosh define the first wave.

beats.title: Creator Channels Professionalize
beats.body: Ray William Johnson, Smosh, nigahiga, Jenna Marbles, and gaming creators show how personality channels can scale into media businesses.

beats.title: PewDiePie Defines the Creator Crown
beats.body: Gaming culture becomes YouTube's central subscriber story as PewDiePie nears the 50 million milestone.

beats.title: Labels and Kids Channels Surge
beats.body: T-Series crosses 100 million and the leaderboard shifts toward music labels, nursery-rhyme networks, and regional entertainment brands.

beats.title: MrBeast Reclaims the Top Spot
beats.body: MrBeast passes T-Series in June 2024, bringing the subscriber crown back to a creator-led channel at massive scale.

beats.title: MrBeast leads the current table
beats.body: MrBeast leads Wikipedia's current most-subscribed channel table with 515 million subscribers.
